title: SDK prototype kits — roadtest notebook
body:
Purpose:
This notebook collects lightweight, reproducible prototype kits (tiny repos + instructions + eval probes) intended for customer-facing rapid validation and internal roadtests. The goal: give a minimal, opinionated path from zero->integrated SDK sample that surfaces the common friction points (auth, retries, streaming, token accounting, telemetry).

Audience:
- Developer advocates running workshops
- Solutions engineers doing quick feasibility checks
- SDK maintainers who want a compact smoke harness for changes
- PMs wanting to validate end-to-end UX improvements quickly

What makes a kit a 'roadtest' kit (opinionated checklist):
- One-command local start (script or docker-compose)
- < 10 files in the repo, easy-to-scan layout
- Includes 3 short scenarios (happy path + 2 failure modes)
- Built-in telemetry hooks (trace id, latency buckets, token usage) with a sample local collector
- CI smoke test that runs in < 90 seconds
- Clear gating recommendations for when to escalate to full integration tests

Kit contents (standard template) — minimal manifest for each kit:
- README.md: one-paragraph description + 4 quick commands
- run.sh / start-local.sh: one command to bootstrap (env hinting)
- app/: tiny sampleapp (Node/Go/Python) that exercises text generation + streaming
- tests/: quick smoke tests (auth, streaming fallback, quota-exceed)
- telemetry/: simple exporter (stdout JSON + optional local OTLP collector)
- ci/: tiny workflow file that runs tests and prints telemetry summary

Quickstart: one-command developer flow (to put in the README)
1) git clone <kit> && cd <kit>
2) cp .env.example .env  # set API_KEY or use local proxy token
3) ./start-local.sh     # starts a mocked or real lightweight backend
4) ./ci/smoke.sh        # runs the three scenarios + prints PASS/FAIL summary
5) open telemetry/output.json to inspect traces and token counts

Three canonical lab scenarios (packaged per kit):
A) Conversational quickreply (happy path)
- Inputs: short user prompt -> expect stable completions under 300ms per token on local test machine (emulated)
- Validate: correct streaming chunks, JSON-lines stable, function-calling stub invoked once

B) Network flakiness (failure mode)
- Simulate: intermittent 503s between token chunks or delayed payloads
- Validate: SDK retries with backoff, streaming reconnection gracefully replays state, user-facing handler sees exactly one final completion event

C) Cost/Quota exhausted (behavioral mode)
- Simulate: pretend quota exceeded mid-response
- Validate: SDK surfaces clear error type (QuotaExceeded), client app shows fallback text, logs token estimate and last-known cursor for safe retry

Telemetry checklist (what each kit captures by default):
- request_id / trace_id propagated across all components (header + logs)
- start_ts, first_token_ts, end_ts (ms precision)
- tokens_requested, tokens_returned, token_cache_hit boolean
- model_name, model_variant (e.g., gpt4o-small-8q), quantization tag if applicable
- error_class (Timeout | TransportError | QuotaExceeded | ModelMismatch)
- simple histogram buckets for latency: 0-50ms, 50-200ms, 200-800ms, 800+ms
Notes: telemetry must be readable in a single JSON file for quick human inspection during a roadtest. OTLP/Prometheus hooks may be present but are optional.

CI smoke tests (examples to include in kit/ci):
- auth-check: call health endpoint with provided token -> exit 1 on 401/403
- streaming-check: open stream, assert we get at least one token within 2s
- fallback-check: trigger simulated 5xx and confirm fallback path emits a specific metric
- token-accounting-check: call with known-output prompt and assert tokens_returned is within +/-10% expected tokens

Failure injection recipes (how to test robustness):
- drop-packets: introduce 100ms-300ms jitter and 10% packet loss in the proxy
- partial-response: truncate body mid-stream to emulate server crash
- delayed-auth: delay auth validation by 5s to simulate KMS latency and observe client timeouts
Include scripts in kit/ci/failures that can toggle these quickly.

Gating and rollout guidance (for SDK maintainers):
- If local roadtest fails streaming-check -> block release and create a minimal repro with trace id + trace file
- If token-accounting drift > 20% -> escalate to model-integration team and run full eval harness
- Passing roadtest is required before promoting sample app to 'examples' repo and adding to quickstart gallery

Workshop runbook (for developer advocates):
- 15min prep: ensure kit runs on laptop (./start-local.sh)
- 5min intro: explain what the kit demonstrates (auth, streaming, telemetry)
- 25min labs: attendees run two scenarios (A+B) in pairs
- 10min debrief: collect friction notes in sticky board (or Slack thread)

Common friction we've seen (notes from prior roadtests):
- env var naming inconsistency (API_KEY vs REDWOOD_API_KEY) -> standardize to REDWOOD_API_KEY
- streaming buffer sizes diverge between example app and production SDK -> include a recommended config snippet
- telemetry verbosity default too high for workshops -> provide a DEBUG flag to toggle detail

Open questions / TODOs (actions and owners):
- (Ethan) build a tiny Docker image that emulates 503 jitter by environment var (due 2025-11-07)
- (Priya) draft the 1-page quickstart that can be used in email outreach (due 2025-11-10)
- (Sofia) add a step in CI to summarize token counts across tests and fail if anomalous (due 2025-11-12)
- Decide: canonical env var naming and add migration note to SDK changelog

Appendix: minimal example smoke.sh output (what we want to see)
-----
AUTH: ok
STREAM: ok (first token 180ms)
FALLBACK: ok (fallback emitted, error_class=QuotaExceeded)
TOKENS: requested=72 returned=69 drift_pct=4.2
TELEMETRY: path=telemetry/output-2025-11-12.json
-----

Notes to self:
- Keep kits intentionally tiny: reduce cognitive load for new users.
- Roadtest kits are not full examples; they are instruments to reveal friction quickly.
- Share a short survey link at the end of every workshop to collect 'where did you get stuck' in 3 bullets.

If this draft looks good I will spin up repo skeletons for Node, Python, and a language-agnostic HTTP proxy example next sprint and assign owners.
